title: Linearity of reduced group action on normalized coefficients asserted, not proved (Lemma 2.3)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body: Lemma 2.3 claims $\bar G\le\mathrm{GL}_n(k)$ acts **linearly** on $k[a_1,\dots,a_n]$ for *every* stratum. The proof is explicit only for the hyperelliptic case; the general argument says $\mathrm{Sym}^d$ is linear and the normalization 'cuts out an affine-linear slice $W_0$' on which the action is $\rho(g)$ times a renormalizing scalar 'which in the classical strata is a root of unity'. Problems: (i) the slice obtained by fixing a prescribed subset of branch points (e.g. $0,\infty$) is $\bar G$-stable only if $\bar G$ preserves that subset; for reduced groups $A_4,S_4,A_5$ (which DO occur for cyclic curves) there is no $\bar G$-invariant 2-element subset of $B$, so the induced map on $(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ is $\rho(g)$ composed with a coordinate-dependent Möbius renormalization and is NOT linear; (ii) 'in the classical strata' silently restricts to the dihedral case; (iii) the explicit weights/permutation for general $(\delta;m_i)$ are never derived (only $w_i=2i\bmod(g+1)$ in the hyperelliptic case).
